stories.title: A locked model trained on nothing but his own sprites
stories.blurb: HaZ Dulull turned his pixel-art game Astro Burn into ten vertical episodes using Nura Studios' Showcraft, and the condition he set was ownership of the training set: a model trained exclusively on his own character sprites, animation and artwork. Voices and music stayed human, and one episode took about a working week end to end.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: This indie dev found a use for AI but says the project was still firmly human led

stories.title: The bartender who could read a drink he had never tasted
stories.blurb: Dan Maccarone builds a whole argument about AI interfaces out of one bar anecdote: a partner who declared a martini perfect on sight, and the drink came back undrinkable. His point is that confidence and accuracy are only loosely coupled, in people and in models, and that the industry is designing for power users who assume everyone is them.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: AI has a hospitality problem money can't fix

stories.title: Calendly rebrands because it stopped being a calendar
stories.blurb: Smith & Diction replaced the neon shapes with something softer, and the trigger was not the logo everyone read as a toilet bowl. Calendly now ships an AI email assistant and a meeting notetaker, and it needs an identity that argues for itself against tools users could vibe-code in an afternoon.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Calendly's finally fixed its toilet bowl of a logo design

stories.title: A wordmark with no single author
stories.blurb: ONBOX built the identity for Vancouver's Bar Supernova around a process rather than a drawing: guests at a pop-up hand-painted a hundred letters, and the modular wordmark is assembled from them. It matches a bar whose kitchen turns other people's food byproducts into shelf-stable ingredients.

sources.name: PRINT Magazine
sources.headline: ONBOX Crowdsourced 100 Letters Hand-Painted at a Pop-Up for Bar Supernova's Crafted Identity

stories.title: Arc'teryx gives its repair infrastructure a front door
stories.blurb: forpeople named and designed System 0, the umbrella that pulls Arc'teryx's product creation, repair services and circular programmes into one customer-facing platform. Arc'teryx creative director Eugenie Frerichs describes the job as translation: turning back-end operations into something a customer can see and use.

stories.title: Being torn apart on the internet is the proof it landed
stories.blurb: Tom Carey watched Newcastle's 2026/27 home shirt get renamed the barcode shirt within hours and reads the pile-on as a compliment. Every summer thousands of clubs unveil kits at once, and few other categories produce an audience willing to argue about the thickness of a stripe.

stories.title: The illustrator who left the meaning to the viewer
stories.blurb: Steven Heller marks the first Brad Holland legacy show, opening at SVA's Gramercy Gallery on 8 September, a year and a half after Holland's death at 81. The case Heller makes is technical: Holland built pictures with deliberate entry points, giving the reader clues rather than a literal restatement of the text.

sources.name: PRINT Magazine
sources.headline: The Daily Heller: The Legacy of Brad Holland, American Illustrator

stories.title: The warehouse for open models changes owner
stories.blurb: Nvidia is reported to be buying Hugging Face for around 12.9 billion dollars, and what it buys is position rather than profit: the site is not yet profitable but has become the default place open-weight models are stored, downloaded and fine-tuned. It arrives as frontier labs build their own silicon to escape Nvidia's leverage.

stories.title: Photoshop gets a second interface, and it is a prompt bar
stories.blurb: Adobe's AI Assisted Editor, in beta, collects the generative tools into one toolbar beside the Pro Editor, and adds markup: draw an arrow or brush a rough shape on the image instead of describing the edit. Firefly Image 5 now reads the whole image context, so masking every region by hand is no longer the price of a local change.

stories.title: Video generation grows a keyframe and a draft mode
stories.blurb: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash extends a scene by reading up to ten seconds of the existing footage instead of the last second, takes first and last frames to interpolate a camera move, and accepts three seconds of external video as a style reference. A 360p draft mode runs at a third of the cost, which is the part that changes how you iterate.
